cells.tense: You are sitting with what you know without rushing it into an answer.
cells.ask: Say one true thing about someone you care for, without softening it or turning it into a question, and let it stand as yours.
cells.core:
You know what you feel, and you're not making it carry anything. That steadiness is the whole thing here. When some pull comes that isn't yours, it lands and it doesn't take, and you go back to what you actually know.
What this rests on is a willingness to go deep on your own — not to perform, not to arrive anywhere, just to follow a line of thought or feeling past the point where it stops being tidy. That kind of depth only comes from understanding that's genuinely yours, and what it gives back is the freedom to see a pattern and walk out of it. Keep feeding it and this stays whole. The cost is showing up for that longer sit when there's nothing to show at the end.

cells.tense: You are reaching past what you know toward a feeling you have not arrived at yet.
cells.ask: Let one conversation this week go wherever it goes, and leave the other person to decide what it becomes next.
cells.core:
You're pushing toward a settled feeling ahead of the feeling itself — trying to land the connection before it's actually here. You keep doing the work that closeness doesn't ask for: re-checking, reading for a sign, testing whether it's still there. And you've already decided how this should turn out, so the moment doesn't get to be what it is.
What's hard is the other person's share of it. Distance, even a little, can read as the whole thing loosening, so you move to close the gap before it has a chance to be ordinary. Letting an ending be an ending, and trusting what comes after without a plan for it, is the way this settles. That takes waiting while things take the shape they take, and it costs the grip you keep on the outcome.

cells.tense: You went quiet at some point and are still standing at a door that has closed.
cells.ask: Write down three things you felt this week, then hand the page to someone as your thinking, not a report on you.
cells.core:
You have something to offer and you're not offering it. When a moment invites presence, you're careful, you wait, and the chance to be here passes. The feeling hasn't gone anywhere; the contact has. No one gets the inside of what you see.
Sorting your own thinking first helps — putting what you've picked up into some order before you show it — but that's not the same as holding it all back. What's short isn't more depth. It's letting someone receive one piece of what you know, badly, before it's sorted at all. Do that once and you keep the full tally. Nothing about it requires you to have more to give than you do today.

cells.tense: You are already keeping what you feel steady in a way you have never claimed as yours.
cells.ask: Name one thing you already hold steady for a person in your life, out loud, as yours to hold.
cells.core:
This is already happening. Something in you keeps feeling steady through things that shake other people, and it keeps connection warm and patient whether or not you say it. You don't say it. It gets described as simply happening, or as someone else's composure, or as a thing you'll know once you find out how you feel.
It's yours. The hard part is that the people closest to you don't know there's a choice being made — so they can't meet the one making it. The simpler form of this is admitting the depth is yours, that you've already understood the pattern and already settled it. Claiming that costs nothing and hands them somebody to answer.
cells.sheetLine: You are already the steady one. You haven't said so.

attempts.check: The draft claim the record will not back is 'what happened there' — naming anyone or anything behind a stopped offering, which the seed stage leaves unstated; drop all of it. The reader can fairly say the past cell guesses at their history and the excess cell makes them defensive, and both would be right, so both name only the mechanism in the present moment they could recognise. The ask holds even if my read is wrong — one unmeasured act of contact and one piece of sorting use nothing and can be refused. The sentence serving me more than the person is 'the authorship is running' — that is the package's vocabulary, and it is cut.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in the last draft was the past cell locating a cause — 'somewhere back there,' a closed door — when the seed stage says only where someone stands, not why. The reader could fairly say the excess cell puts a hidden motive in their head and the quiet cell guesses at their history; both now name only the mechanism in a moment they could recognise. The asks survive being wrong: each is one visible act, costs nothing, and can be refused without the reading collapsing. The sentence serving the writer was 'the knowing' and its cousins — verbs dressed as nouns — and every one is cut.
